dispositions.reason: Part A's new scored-heading mechanism closes the inherited false-negative but opens a fresh false-positive class: NOISE_DISCOUNTED only checks whether noise-stripping changed anything within a 200-char lookback, without requiring the discounted noise to belong to the same boundary as the candidate. A genuine footnote glued to an unrelated earlier sentence's closing delimiter, sitting on the line before an ordinary in-text section citation, reaches the acceptance threshold and launders that citation into a false SECTION heading, re-parenting a real lettered clause under it. Reproduced under two materially different combinations; isolation control (removing only the glued digit) reverts to correct behavior, confirming causation.

The whitespace-normalization root-cause fix and the canonical resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence primitive are genuinely robust when the getDefinition tool is actually invoked. But evidenceUnresolved is only ever set inside that tool's own execution - it requires the model to call it. caller.ts's summarizeContextBundle dumps CovenantContextBundle items' raw excerptText verbatim into the model's first turn, inviting an answer from that context with zero tool calls; ContextItem carries no operative-state/supersession field. An end-to-end reproduction (a real CONFLICTED definition with competing $9M/$12M amendments, stale $5M text embedded in the context bundle, a scripted model that submits sufficiency:COMPLETE with zero tool calls) yields compileCovenantToIR status COMPLETED with no OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED, and verifyCompiledCandidate on that result yields VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND - exactly the outcome Part A's design principle claims is unreachable.

Oxford-comma delimiter recognition, the narrowed restated-modal guard, and the linear-time incremental-Set scanning all held under fresh adversarial construction: mixed Oxford+restated-modal combinations, a novel false-positive control, nested parentheticals, and an independent linear-scaling re-measurement (slope ~1.00/0.98) confirming the quadratic-complexity fix.

Code inspection passes the disqualifying bar: condition-suspicion-classifier.ts's system prompt is genuinely compositional (role-based reasoning, zero regex/word lists), and verify.ts's two-gate routing matches its own documentation - no path can skip review without an explicit successful NO_MATERIAL_CONDITION_SUSPECTED from Gate 2. But the deciding empirical claim - real semantic generalization on 22 fresh, never-seen condition constructions - could not be validated: the account-level Vercel AI Gateway budget was already exhausted ($50.05/$50.00) before this recertification began, so all 22 real classifyConditionSuspicion() calls and an independent raw HTTP probe returned HTTP 402 (real cost incurred: $0.00). Every call fail-safed to UNCERTAIN, producing 100% routing-to-review, but this is the fail-safe path, not genuine model judgment - it does not validate Part A's central disclosed limitation. Per this exact defect class's history (four prior recertifications failed on unvalidated empirical claims), architecture inspection alone is insufficient grounds for closure.

dispositions.reason: 7 consecutive clean runs against real, unmocked local Postgres covering multi-object races, a three-generation flux race (zombie/legitimate/reclaim) across single and 4 concurrent objects, and a dedicated 25-way deadlock-risk probe (never hung, 122-146ms). No stale write ever took effect. The parent-row SELECT...FOR UPDATE lock serializes concurrent per-object writes without deadlocking and incidentally also prevents a same-object create/create race.

Part A correctly wrapped the last-resort console.error in try/catch, closing the reported reproduction. But classifyError, called before console.error at both call sites, can itself throw via a poisoned error value's toString()/.message getter - a new, different sub-defect one statement earlier in the same call chain, still capable of producing a completely silent failure.
